12.head: 717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b
12.feedback: {"head":"717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b","verdict":"pass","summary":"The change adds a Node-only, read-only reporter (scripts/factory/diagnostics.cjs) invoked only on a failed Claude model step, which builds a bounded, allowlist-only JSON report (fixed tool names, fixed command categories/forms, counts, stop reason) from the pinned action's temporary execution file and uploads it under a separate \"diagnostic-<phase>-<grantId>\" artifact name with 7-day retention. Verified against the current source: the reporter is copied into $RUNNER_TEMP/factory-control before the untrusted ticket head is checked out (same trust boundary already used for worker.cjs), so it cannot be tampered with by ticket/repo content. It correctly distinguishes \"denials array present but empty\" (status=available, denialCount=0) from \"denials missing/invalid\" (status=unavailable, denialCount=null, explicit reason) — never fabricating a zero. File reads are bounded (8 MiB, re-checked after fstat to avoid TOCTOU growth), symlinks/directories are rejected via lstat+O_NOFOLLOW, and the output file is written with O_EXCL so a pre-existing file is refused rather than overwritten. Only three fixed-shape fields (tool, commandCategory, commandForm) ever leave the reporter per denial; raw commands/paths/prompts/IDs/errors are never included, verified by tests that smuggle a synthetic secret through every untrusted field and assert it never appears in the report, stdout, or stderr. The new workflow steps use `continue-on-error: true` and `if: failure() && steps.model.outcome == 'failure'`, so they only fire on an actual model-step failure, can't themselves flip the job back to success, and are skipped for preflight failures or cancellations — confirmed against factory-cycle.yml/factory-pr-review.yml, which gate on job `.result` unaffected by this addition. No other file (policy.cjs, worker.cjs, controller.cjs, permissions blocks, FACTORY_ENABLED gate, turn-ceiling logic) was touched. The new test file is automatically picked up by the existing `yarn test:factory` glob already run in CI, so no CI wiring changes were needed. Regression coverage is strong: missing/oversized/malformed/symlinked/directory inputs, truncation at 100 denials, PowerShell command classification, exact-vs-with-arguments vs compound/dynamic command forms, and non-overwrite of an existing output file are all exercised.","findings":[]}

14.head: e117eb47a992b5be679f1da0db858e6ede25fda6
14.feedback: {"head":"e117eb47a992b5be679f1da0db858e6ede25fda6","verdict":"pass","summary":"The diff raises FACTORY_MAX_TURNS_PER_RUN's ceiling to 50 and FACTORY_MAX_TICKETS_PER_DAY's ceiling to 5 in scripts/factory/policy.cjs's LIMITS table, with matching bound checks via the existing integer()/readConfig() validation (rejects 51/6 and malformed/missing values, same as before for the old ceilings of 20/2). New tests cover: turn budgets up to 50 remaining usable while preserving other caps; values above 50 or malformed being rejected; disabled/zero-turn budgets still blocking work; five admissions in one Bucharest day including an owner-PR review ticket, with a sixth ticket refused until midnight; and retrying an already-admitted ticket not re-admitting it or refunding its lifetime coding/retry counters. factory-worker.test.cjs confirms both coding and review CLI invocations carry --max-turns 50 without gaining extra tools. factory-controller.test.cjs's disabled validate-only smoke test and factory-ci.yml's CI fixture both exercise 50/5 with FACTORY_ENABLED=false, no token, no state writes, and no inference, matching the \"ordinary CI without inference or real credentials\" criterion. docs/CLAUDE-FACTORY.md documents the rollout sequence (stay at 20/2 until the policy PR is reviewed on trusted main, then move to 50/5 with the factory still disabled) and the follow-on issue #11 controlled-retry plan, without actually triggering any model session, merge, or live ledger change. All other policy invariants (15-minute timeout, 2 coding attempts/1 retry, 2 reviews, 1 concurrent ticket, OAuth-only subscription auth, review gate, PR #13 diagnostics) are untouched in the reviewed code. I did not find any violation of policy boundaries, scope creep beyond the two ceilings, or evidence that live credentials/state were touched.","findings":[]}

16.head: 007e082825c56770966fd06ad1d16faeed9e2ebb
16.feedback: {"head":"007e082825c56770966fd06ad1d16faeed9e2ebb","verdict":"pass","summary":"The diff raises the FACTORY_MAX_TURNS_PER_RUN policy cap in scripts/factory/policy.cjs from 50 to 100, with accompanying test updates in factory-policy.test.cjs (accepts 1/20/50/100, rejects 101/999/-1/1.5/\"100x\"/empty/undefined), factory-worker.test.cjs (confirms both code and review buildArgs receive --max-turns 100 without any tool/permission changes), and factory-controller.test.cjs (disabled 100-turn/5-ticket validate-only smoke test). The CI workflow's disabled validation fixture and docs were updated to exercise/describe the new ceiling. Crucially, no live GitHub Actions repository variable is touched by this diff — all operational workflows (factory-agents.yml, factory-cycle.yml) read FACTORY_* values from `vars.*` context, not from committed code, so the actual deployed turn ceiling remains governed by the repo variable the owner controls, consistent with the ticket's requirement to keep the live setting at 50 and FACTORY_ENABLED=false until independent review and merge. The docs (CLAUDE-FACTORY.md) correctly state current main's live value stays 50 pending review, and preserve all other limits (daily=5, coding=2, reviews=2, retries=1, concurrency=1, timeout=15m, OAuth-only auth). The new plan file and docs explicitly reiterate that issue #11 remains blocked/exhausted (coding=2, retries=1, reviews=0, no PR) and must not be re-dispatched, reset, or given a replacement admission — matching the ticket's explicit prohibition. No tool permissions, authentication mechanism, or other durable counters were altered.","findings":[]}

18.head: b883586f30756fbc80c82193a0244e6f67b5bb5c
18.feedback: {"head":"b883586f30756fbc80c82193a0244e6f67b5bb5c","verdict":"changes_requested","summary":"The branch correctly implements ticket #18's single-use, owner-only `recover` operation for issue #11 (scripts/factory/recovery.cjs, policy.cjs/controller.cjs integration, factory-recovery.test.cjs, worker command-guidance docs): eligibility and ledger validation are pinned to the exact criteria hash and the two historical blocked grant IDs, only the coding-attempt ceiling is bypassed for one extra reservation, old grants/admission/retry counters are preserved, the new attempt starts from current main, and tool permissions/`--allowedTools` strings are unchanged. That part matches the previously-passed review at 40eb635 and its two carried-over minor gaps remain unresolved. However, the head commit (b883586, \"Report the required review gate through a real pull request job\") adds a large, entirely unrelated feature set for a different ticket (#20 / PR #19 \"gate-reporting\" bootstrap): a new `factory-review-status.yml` workflow, `scripts/factory/gate-report.cjs` (which calls the mutating `rerun-failed-jobs` Actions API), a `GitHub.request` behavior change, controller changes to the review-gate check name/refresh flow, and `actions: write` permission grants added to three existing workflows (factory-cycle.yml, factory-pr-review.yml, factory-review-gate.yml). None of this is described, required, or even mentioned by ticket #18's text, and the accompanying plan doc explicitly frames it as repairing issue #20 inside PR #19 with its own unfinished checklist. This is out-of-scope work bundled into the ticket-18 branch/PR, including a real permission escalation across multiple workflows, and should not be approved as part of this ticket's review.","findings":[{"severity":"critical","message":"The diff for this PR/branch bundles a second, unrelated feature (ticket #20 / PR #19 'gate reporting' bootstrap: new .github/workflows/factory-review-status.yml, scripts/factory/gate-report.cjs, controller.cjs gate-refresh wiring, github.cjs response-parsing change, and docs/superpowers plan+spec files) on top of the issue-11 recovery work. Ticket #18's body says nothing about gate reporting, PR #19, or issue #20, and the task instructions require working only on the ticket's own criteria. Mixing an unrelated, separately-scoped change into this PR means it has not gone through its own authorized review/ticket process and should be split out, not merged under ticket #18's review."},{"severity":"important","message":"As part of the unrelated gate-reporting bundle, commit b883586 grants `actions: write` permission to three existing workflows (factory-cycle.yml, factory-pr-review.yml, factory-review-gate.yml) that previously had only `actions: read`, and adds scripts/factory/gate-report.cjs which performs a mutating `POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` call. This is a real permission/policy expansion of the automation's capabilities that is not justified by, or in scope of, ticket #18's recovery requirements and was not reviewed as such."},{"severity":"minor","message":"Carried over from the prior review of 40eb635 (unchanged in this diff): recovery.cjs's assertEligible/allowance only check config.reviews >= 1 / config.daily >= 1 rather than pinning to the exact deployed values (2 and 5) the way config.coding and config.retries are pinned. Currently harmless since deployed vars keep reviews=2/daily=5, but it's an asymmetry versus the ticket's 'fail closed for lower configured budgets' requirement."},{"severity":"minor","message":"Carried over from the prior review: the hardcoded CRITERIA hash and the two PRIOR grant IDs/run IDs in scripts/factory/recovery.cjs were computed against a frozen local fixture and have not been verified here against the live ledger/issue #11 body. A mismatch would just cause a safe refusal, but this should be confirmed once before any real owner recovery dispatch."}]}
